newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama prepares for takeover of canal.
newsitem.headline: Panama prepares for takeover of canal.

text.p: Panamanian President Ernesto Perez Balladares signed into law on Wednesday legislation which will govern the operations of the Panama canal after the United States hands it over to Panama on Dec. 31, 1999.

"Today Panama puts into force for the first time in its history legislation that will regulate all the canal activities, in order for the canal to be transferred effectively (to Panama)," Perez Balladares told reporters.
The president sought to reassure the international community that Panama was prepared for the running of the 51-mile waterway, one of the world's most important.

"Panama tells the world today that it is preparing for the administration of the canal and it informs its clients that the passage through the trans-oceanic will not be disrupted," Perez Balladares added. He said the canal would be run as efficiently or more efficiently than prior to the handover, and that it will be administered by an independent authority.
The law, which takes effect once the canal is returned to Panama, will create the Panama Canal Authority and replace the Panama Canal Commission (PCC) and all U.S. laws.
Under the 1977 Panama Canal Treaty, the United States is to turn over operation of the canal and eight military bases to Panamanian control and withdraw all troops by Dec. 31, 1999.
